findings.title: Review counts are explicitly left without the noise floor the plan requires
findings.description: The design excludes a review noise floor and proposes labeling review figures “no floor measured.” But the architecture says LLM-derived review signals carry their own noise floor, and the 403 slice-plan success criteria require LLM-sourced numbers to be shown against their noise floor. Labeling the missing floor is transparent, but does not meet that requirement; the design needs to provide the floor or resolve the scope mismatch with the architecture and plan.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/403-slice.slice-ranges-and-rollup-reports.md#D8 — Each figure carries its source, sample size and noise floor state

findings.title: Fast-forward boundaries can include changes already on the target
findings.description: The claim that a fast-forward is possible only if the target has not moved past the fork is not generally true. A slice branch can merge newer target work into itself, then be fast-forwarded into the target because the target commit is now an ancestor of the slice tip. In that case, using the original reflog fork as `before_sha` includes changes that were already on the target before the landing. This can misattribute unrelated work to the slice and undermine the architecture’s before/after measurement goal. Define how the resolver identifies the actual target state before landing, or explicitly refuse the case it cannot resolve accurately; add a test for a sync-merged branch that is subsequently fast-forwarded.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/403-slice.slice-ranges-and-rollup-reports.md#D3 — Before and after are the target just before and just after the landing

findings.title: `report history` does not specify handling for its Git history lookup failures
findings.description: `report history` orders snapshots by the target’s first-parent history, which requires a Git history lookup. The failure-mode table covers archive/revision failures and range-resolver failures, but does not state what happens if this history lookup hangs, returns non-zero, or otherwise cannot provide an answer. Specify an explicit handling strategy and observable signal, consistent with the requirement that a failed Git query is never treated as a valid empty result.
